Information received since the September meeting points to a still-strong labor market and moderate growth, but with weak business fixed investment and exports and inflation below 2%. In New Keynesian frameworks (e.g., Galí and Gertler 1999; Woodford 2003; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans 2005), low realized inflation and subdued expectations strengthen the case for accommodative policy to stabilize the output gap. The Committee’s rate cut and ample-reserves operations (T-bill purchases and repos) align with evidence that monetary easing works through the interest-rate and liquidity channels to support real activity (Sims 1992), and can be especially helpful where investment is sensitive to financing conditions and internal funds (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994). Even so, the noted weakness in capex and external demand tempers the outlook. Net tone: mildly positive but cautious.
